title: Which of the two angles is greater?
description: Angle AOB is laid over angle XOY with the vertex O on the vertex O. The arm OA falls on OX and the arm OB falls on OY, so the same turn makes both angles. Keeko's doubt is that the angle with the longer arms is greater.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the vertices overlap and both pairs of arms lie on top of each other, the angles are equal. Watch for students who think longer arms make a greater angle.

source: Now consider ∠AOB and ∠XOY in the figure. Which is greater?
video_script.why: The child sees that two angles whose vertex and arms overlap exactly are equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's own pair of angles AOB and XOY
video_script.anchor: the angles AOB and XOY of the book, one laid over the other
video_script.wrong_answer: the angle with the longer arms is greater
video_script.wrong_move: judges an angle by how long its arms are drawn
video_script.payoff_line: Neither angle is greater, the two angles are equal

final_answer.value: neither is greater; the angles are equal
final_answer.spoken: neither angle is greater, the two angles are equal

maths_rules: superimpose: vertex O of one angle on vertex O of the other
arm OA falls on arm OX, and arm OB falls on arm OY
the vertex and both pairs of arms lie on top of each other, so the angles are equal in size
the same amount of turn moves OB to OA and OY to OX
slip: the length of the arms does not change the angle
video_script.design: One idea: superimpose, and if the vertex and both pairs of arms overlap, the angles are equal. The two angles of the book stay on the board all video. Keeko's doubt: longer arms mean a greater angle.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Neither angle is greater, the two angles are equal
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Neither angle is greater, the two angles are equal.
The vertex and both pairs of arms lie on top of each other.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the long arms of one angle are cut back to the length of the short arms and the opening stays the same

marks.doubt: the angle with the longer arms is circled
marks.cut: the long arms are cut back to the short length
marks.same: the opening is seen to be unchanged

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the angle with the longer arms is greater.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>But cut the long arms back to the short length. The opening does not change at all.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The length of the arms shows how far they are drawn, not how much they have turned.
